proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a linear extension \(\pi\in\Pi_{\preceq}\), and write
\[
 S=\operatorname{Pred}_{\pi}(T).
\]
Because \(\Gamma\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\), its modified Cholesky factorization in the order \(\pi\) exists uniquely:
\[
 \Gamma=L_{\pi}D_{\pi}^{2}L_{\pi}^{\top},
\]
where \(L_{\pi}\) is unit lower triangular in that order and \(D_{\pi}\) has strictly positive diagonal.  Let \(Z\sim N(0,I_p)\) and realize the Gaussian divisor as \(G_{\Gamma}=L_{\pi}D_{\pi}Z\).  If \(Y\notin S\), the residual of \((G_{\Gamma})_T\) after linear projection on \((G_{\Gamma})_S\) is \((D_{\pi})_{TT}Z_T\).  Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac{\gamma_{YT\cdot S}(\Gamma)}{\gamma_{TT\cdot S}(\Gamma)}
 &=\frac{\operatorname{Cov}\!\left((G_{\Gamma})_Y,(D_{\pi})_{TT}Z_T\right)}
         {\operatorname{Var}\!\left((D_{\pi})_{TT}Z_T\right)}\\
 &=\frac{(L_{\pi})_{YT}(D_{\pi})_{TT}^{2}}
         {(D_{\pi})_{TT}^{2}}
 =(L_{\pi})_{YT}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The division is legitimate because
\(\gamma_{TT\cdot S}(\Gamma)>0\): it is the Schur complement of the positive-definite principal block \(\Gamma_{SS}\), with the stated empty-set convention when \(S=\varnothing\).  If \(Y\in S\), conditioning on \(S\) makes \(\gamma_{YT\cdot S}(\Gamma)=0\), and triangularity gives \((L_{\pi})_{YT}=0\), so the same identity remains valid.

This identity proves the relation between the causal target and the observable covariance functional; it does not define that relation.  Indeed, by \(U=AH\), the full-column-rank condition on \(A\) gives a deterministic left inverse of \(A\), hence \(H\) is a measurable linear function of \(U\).  Thus \(U\perp G_{\Gamma}\) implies \(H\perp Z\).  Multiplying the equality \(X=AH+L_{\pi}D_{\pi}Z\) by \(L_{\pi}^{-1}\) gives the acyclic structural system
\[
 X=(I-L_{\pi}^{-1})X+L_{\pi}^{-1}AH+D_{\pi}Z.
\]
Its coefficient matrix is strictly lower triangular in the order \(\pi\), and its total directed-effect matrix is
\[
 \{I-(I-L_{\pi}^{-1})\}^{-1}=L_{\pi}.
\]
Consequently, surgical intervention on coordinate \(T\) changes the mean of coordinate \(Y\) at derivative \((L_{\pi})_{YT}\).  Premultiplication by the invertible matrix \(L_{\pi}^{-1}\) preserves the rank of the source loading, and the source independence and nonconstancy conditions are unchanged.  The greatest-divisor assumption makes the \(\Gamma\) used in this construction the stipulated law-indexed causal Gaussian covariance.

It remains to determine all possible sets \(S\).  Every predecessor set of \(T\) contains
\(D=\{v:v\prec T\}\), contains no strict successor of \(T\), and hence has the form \(D\cup J\) for some \(J\subseteq A\).  If \(w\in J\) and \(v\in A\) satisfies \(v\prec w\), then \(v\) precedes \(T\) in \(\pi\), so \(v\in J\).  Thus \(J\) is an ideal of \(\preceq|_A\).  Conversely, take \(J\in\mathcal J\).  The sets \(D\cup J\) and \(D\cup J\cup\{T\}\) are ideals of the full partial order: a predecessor of an element of \(D\) lies in \(D\); a predecessor of an element of \(J\) lies in \(D\cup J\); and every predecessor of \(T\) lies in \(D\).  Hence one may take a linear extension of \(D\cup J\), then place \(T\), and then take a linear extension of the complement.  This realizes \(D\cup J\) as exactly \(\operatorname{Pred}_{\pi}(T)\).  Substitution into the regression identity proves
\[
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)
 =\{\beta_J(\Gamma):J\in\mathcal J\}.
\]

For the singleton characterization, let \(J\to J\cup\{W\}\) be an ideal edge, set \(S=D\cup J\), and abbreviate
\[
 u=\gamma_{TT\cdot S},\qquad
 v=\gamma_{WW\cdot S},\qquad
 r=\gamma_{TW\cdot S},\qquad
 d=\gamma_{YT\cdot S},\qquad
 e=\gamma_{YW\cdot S},
\]
where every quantity is evaluated at \(\Gamma\).  Positive definiteness gives
\[
 u>0,\qquad v>0,\qquad uv-r^2>0.
\]
Schur complementation on \(W\) yields
\[
 \gamma_{YT\cdot(S\cup\{W\})}=d-\frac{re}{v},
 \qquad
 \gamma_{TT\cdot(S\cup\{W\})}=u-\frac{r^2}{v}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \beta_J-\beta_{J\cup\{W\}}
 &=\frac d u-\frac{d-re/v}{u-r^2/v}\\
 &=\frac{r(ue-dr)}{u(uv-r^2)}\\
 &=\frac{r\{e-dr/u\}}{uv-r^2}\\
 &=\frac{\gamma_{TW\cdot S}(\Gamma)
          \gamma_{YW\cdot(S\cup\{T\})}(\Gamma)}
         {uv-r^2}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The positive denominator shows that adjacent ideal values agree if and only if the product in the proposition vanishes.  The undirected graph of ideals is connected: from any nonempty ideal, deleting a maximal element leaves an ideal, and repeated deletion reaches \(\varnothing\).  Hence vanishing of every edge product makes all \(\beta_J\) equal.  Conversely, if the fiber is a singleton, every adjacent pair is equal, so every edge product vanishes.  If \(W=Y\), the second factor is the strictly positive conditional variance \(\gamma_{YY\cdot(S\cup\{T\})}\); if \(Y\in S\), both adjacent coefficients and the relevant conditional covariance are zero.  Thus no overlap, swap-margin, or genericity condition is being used at collision or boundary strata.

We construct the laws and verify each defining condition.  Fix
\[
 m=6,\qquad \eta=\frac1{10},\qquad \kappa=\frac1{20},
\]
and define
\[
 f_0(x)=(1-\eta)\frac{e^{-\sqrt2|x|}}{\sqrt2}
       +\eta c_6(1+x^2)^{-6},
 \qquad c_6=\frac{256}{63\pi}.
\]
The identities
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}\frac{e^{-\sqrt2|x|}}{\sqrt2}\,dx=1,
 \qquad
 \int_{\mathbb R}(1+x^2)^{-6}\,dx
 =\frac{\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma(11/2)}{\Gamma(6)}
 =\frac{63\pi}{256}
\]
show that \(f_0\) is an even probability density.  Applying the gamma-integral representation of \((1+x^2)^{-6}\) and then the Gaussian Fourier integral gives
\[
 \phi_0(t)=\frac{1-\eta}{1+t^2/2}
 +\eta e^{-|t|}P_5(|t|),
\]
where
\[
 P_5(z)=1+z+\frac{4z^2}{9}+\frac{z^3}{9}
       +\frac{z^4}{63}+\frac{z^5}{945}.
\]
All coefficients are positive, so \(\phi_0(t)>0\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\).

Choose an even \(C^\infty\) function \(\chi:\mathbb R\to[0,1]\) equal to one on \([-1,1]\) and zero off \([-2,2]\).  For \(M\ge1\), put
\[
 \delta=\kappa M^{-2},\qquad
 \phi_{1,M}(t)=\phi_0(t)
 \left[1+\chi(t/M)\{e^{-\delta t^2/2}-1\}\right].
\]
Let \(\varphi_\delta\) denote the centered Gaussian density of variance \(\delta\), and define
\[
 \widehat h_M(t)=\phi_0(t)\{1-\chi(t/M)\}
                         \{1-e^{-\delta t^2/2}\},
 \qquad
 f_{1,M}=f_0*\varphi_\delta+h_M.
\]
The Fourier transform of the displayed candidate is exactly \(\phi_{1,M}\).

We next prove that it is nonnegative.  With
\[
 b_M(z)=M^2\phi_0(Mz)\{1-\chi(z)\}
                    \{1-e^{-\kappa z^2/2}\},
\]
Fourier inversion gives
\[
 h_M(x)=\frac1{2\pi M}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-iMxz}b_M(z)\,dz.
\]
For every integer \(0\le j\le12\), there is a constant \(B_j<\infty\), independent of \(M\ge1\), such that
\[
 \|b_M^{(j)}\|_1\le B_j.
\]
To verify this uniformly, note first that \(1-\chi\) vanishes on \(|z|\le1\).  On \(|z|\ge1\), for every \(0\le\ell\le12\), differentiation of the rational term gives
\[
 \left|\partial_z^\ell
   \frac{M^2}{1+M^2z^2/2}\right|
 =\left|\partial_z^\ell
   \frac{2}{z^2+2M^{-2}}\right|
 \le C_\ell |z|^{-2-\ell}.
\]
Every derivative of the Student Fourier term \(M^2e^{-M|z|}P_5(M|z|)\), away from zero, is a finite sum of terms bounded by
\[
 M^{2+\ell+r}|z|^r e^{-M|z|}
 =|z|^{-2-\ell}(M|z|)^{2+\ell+r}e^{-M|z|},
\]
with \(r\) in a fixed finite set.  Since \(M|z|\ge1\) and
\(\sup_{y\ge1}y^a e^{-y}<\infty\) for fixed \(a\), these terms are bounded by an integrable multiple of \(|z|^{-2-\ell}\), uniformly in \(M\).  Derivatives of \(1-\chi\) are supported on \(1\le|z|\le2\), and every derivative of \(1-e^{-\kappa z^2/2}\) is bounded.  The product rule proves the asserted \(L^1\) bounds.

Using the cases \(j=0\) and \(j=12\), and integrating by parts twelve times in the latter case, gives
\[
 |h_M(x)|
 \le \frac1{2\pi M}
 \min\!\left(B_0,\frac{B_{12}}{|Mx|^{12}}\right)
 \le A_{12}M^{-1}(1+M|x|)^{-12}
\]
for a constant \(A_{12}\) independent of \(M\).  Since \(\delta\le1\), retaining only the Student component and restricting the Gaussian convolution variable to \([-1,1]\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (f_0*\varphi_\delta)(x)
 &\ge \eta c_6 3^{-6}(1+x^2)^{-6}
       \Pr\{|N(0,\delta)|\le1\}\\
 &\ge a_6(1+x^2)^{-6},
 \qquad a_6=\eta c_6 3^{-7}>0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here \(1+(x-z)^2\le3(1+x^2)\) for \(|z|\le1\), and
\(\Pr\{|N(0,\delta)|\le1\}\ge\Pr\{|N(0,1)|\le1\}>1/3\).  Because
\[
 (1+x^2)^6\le(1+M|x|)^{12}\qquad(M\ge1),
\]
we obtain
\[
 \frac{|h_M(x)|}{(f_0*\varphi_\delta)(x)}
 \le\frac{A_{12}}{a_6M}.
\]
Thus \(f_{1,M}\ge0\) for all \(M\ge2A_{12}/a_6\).  Moreover, \(\widehat h_M(0)=0\), so \(f_{1,M}\) integrates to one; it is even and hence centered.  The compensated construction is in the scalar fixed-envelope tradition of \cite{Meister2006}, while the positivity verification above is specific to the present splice.

The spatial bound implies \(\int |x|^j|h_M(x)|\,dx<\infty\) for \(0\le j\le8\).  Since \(\widehat h_M\) vanishes on a neighborhood of zero, differentiation at zero gives
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}x^j h_M(x)\,dx=0,
 \qquad 0\le j\le8.
\]
If \(S_6\) has density \(c_6(1+x^2)^{-6}\), beta integration yields
\[
 \mathbb E S_6^{2j}
 =\frac{\Gamma(j+1/2)\Gamma(11/2-j)}
        {\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma(11/2)},
 \qquad 0\le j\le5.
\]
Combining this with the standardized-Laplace moments \((2j)!/2^j\), the even moments of \(f_0\) through order eight are
\[
 \mu_2=\frac{41}{45},\qquad
 \mu_4=\frac{227}{42},\qquad
 \mu_6=\frac{17011}{210},\qquad
 \mu_8=\frac{204121}{90}.
\]
Let \(H_0\) have density \(f_0\), and let \(H_{1,M}\) have density \(f_{1,M}\).  The vanishing moments of \(h_M\) show that the moments of \(H_{1,M}\) through order eight equal those of \(H_0+N(0,\delta)\).  Hence, for \(0\le\delta\le1\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E H_{1,M}^8
 &=\mu_8+28\delta\mu_6+210\delta^2\mu_4
   +420\delta^3\mu_2+105\delta^4\\
 &\le\frac{554293}{90}.
 \end{aligned}
\]

The splice multiplier lies in \([e^{-2\kappa},1]\): if \(\chi(t/M)\ne0\), then \(|t|\le2M\), so \(e^{-\delta t^2/2}\ge e^{-2\kappa}\), and outside that support the multiplier is one.  The positive rational component of \(\phi_0\) therefore implies that both \(\phi_0\) and \(\phi_{1,M}\) are bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of \(|t|^{-2}\) for all sufficiently large \(|t|\), uniformly in large \(M\).  If either scalar law had a Gaussian convolution divisor of variance \(r>0\), the residual factor would have modulus
\[
 e^{rt^2/2}|\phi(t)|,
\]
which diverges as \(|t|\to\infty\), contradicting the unit modulus bound for a characteristic function.  Thus both scalar sources are Gaussian-indecomposable.

We now establish indistinguishability, including the order-six weighted Fourier estimate.  Fix \(v=1/10\) and set
\[
 q_{0,M}=f_0*\varphi_{v+\delta},\qquad
 q_{1,M}=f_{1,M}*\varphi_v,
 \qquad D_M=q_{1,M}-q_{0,M}.
\]
Then
\[
 \widehat D_M(t)=e^{-vt^2/2}\phi_0(t)
 \{1-\chi(t/M)\}\{1-e^{-\delta t^2/2}\},
\]
so \(\widehat D_M\) vanishes on \([-M,M]\).  Retaining the Student component in \(q_{0,M}\) and restricting the Gaussian convolution variable to a fixed compact interval gives a constant \(a_v>0\), uniform in \(0\le\delta\le\kappa\), such that
\[
 q_{0,M}(x)\ge a_v(1+x^2)^{-6}.
\]
Because \(f_0\) has a finite sixth absolute moment,
\[
 \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|\phi_0^{(\ell)}(t)|
 \le\mathbb E|H_0|^\ell<\infty,
 \qquad 0\le\ell\le6.
\]
For \(r\ge1\), derivatives of \(1-\chi(t/M)\) are bounded by constants times \(M^{-r}\) and supported on \(M\le|t|\le2M\); the zeroth derivative vanishes on \(|t|\le M\).  Also, for \(0\le r\le6\),
\[
 \sup_{M\ge1,t\in\mathbb R}
 \left|\partial_t^r\{1-e^{-\kappa t^2/(2M^2)}\}\right|<\infty,
\]
because for \(r\ge1\) the derivative is \(M^{-r}\) times a fixed polynomial in \(t/M\) times a Gaussian, while the zeroth derivative is at most one.  Finally, each derivative of \(e^{-vt^2/2}\) is a polynomial, of degree no larger than the derivative order, times the same Gaussian.  The product rule therefore gives constants \(C_j<\infty\), fixed independently of \(M\), such that
\[
 |\widehat D_M^{(j)}(t)|
 \le C_j(1+|t|)^j e^{-vt^2/2}
       \mathbf 1\{|t|\ge M\},
 \qquad 0\le j\le6.
\]
In particular, every displayed derivative lies in \(L^2(\mathbb R)\).  The distributional Fourier identity
\(\widehat{x^jD_M}=i^{-j}\widehat D_M^{(j)}\), first for smooth compactly supported Fourier truncations and then by \(L^2\) passage, together with \(\mathrm{lem:parseval\text{-}identity}\), yields
\[
 \|x^jD_M\|_2^2
 =\frac1{2\pi}\|\widehat D_M^{(j)}\|_2^2,
 \qquad 0\le j\le6.
\]
Expanding the weight and applying this identity term by term gives the exact formula
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}(1+x^2)^6|D_M(x)|^2\,dx
 =\frac1{2\pi}\sum_{j=0}^{6}\binom6j
   \|\widehat D_M^{(j)}\|_2^2.
\]
For \(M\ge1\), integration by parts in the Gaussian tail gives, uniformly for \(0\le j\le6\),
\[
 \int_{|t|\ge M}(1+|t|)^{2j}e^{-vt^2}\,dt
 \le C'_j(1+M)^{12}e^{-vM^2}.
\]
The lower density bound and the weighted identity now imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \chi^2(q_{1,M},q_{0,M})
 &=\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{|D_M(x)|^2}{q_{0,M}(x)}\,dx\\
 &\le A(1+M)^{12}e^{-vM^2}
 \end{aligned}
\]
for a fixed \(A<\infty\).

Independence and Fubini give the product identity
\[
 1+\chi^2(q_{1,M}^{\otimes N},q_{0,M}^{\otimes N})
 =\{1+\chi^2(q_{1,M},q_{0,M})\}^{N}.
\]
Choose \(M^2=30\log N\).  Since \(vM^2=3\log N\),
\[
 N\chi^2(q_{1,M},q_{0,M})
 \le A N^{-2}(1+\sqrt{30\log N})^{12}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus the product chi-square divergence tends to zero.  Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the likelihood-ratio difference gives
\[
 \|q_{1,M}^{\otimes N}-q_{0,M}^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\frac12
 \sqrt{\chi^2(q_{1,M}^{\otimes N},q_{0,M}^{\otimes N})}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]

Embed the scalar experiment into three dimensions.  Let
\[
 a=(1,2/5,1)^\top,qquad
 \overline\Gamma=\Gamma_\star-vaa^\top.
\]
The leading principal minors of \(\overline\Gamma\) are
\[
 \frac9{10},\qquad \frac{189}{250},\qquad \frac{294}{625},
\]
so Sylvester's criterion gives \(\overline\Gamma\succ0\).  Apply to both scalar laws the same Markov kernel \(z\mapsto az+G_{\overline\Gamma}\).  Total variation contracts under a Markov kernel, since the image likelihood ratio is a conditional expectation and the \(L^1\) norm contracts.  The two image laws are
\[
 P_{0,N}=\mathcal L(aH_{1,M}+G_{\Gamma_\star}),
 \qquad
 P_{1,N}=\mathcal L(aH_0+G_{\Gamma_\star+\delta aa^\top}).
\]
They are Borel laws because they have convolution densities.  Consequently,
\[
 \|P_{0,N}^{\otimes N}-P_{1,N}^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
The selected cutoff gives
\[
 s_N=\delta=\frac{\kappa}{M^2}
 =\frac1{600\log N}.
\]

We verify the fixed-class constants.  The leading principal minors of
\(\Gamma_\star-I/10\) are
\[
 \frac9{10},\qquad \frac{13}{20},\qquad \frac{8109}{25000},
\]
and those of \(4I-\Gamma(1)\) are
\[
 2,\qquad \frac{126}{25},\qquad \frac{44}{125}.
\]
Since \(\Gamma(s)\) is increasing in Loewner order, the endpoint inequalities and Sylvester's criterion imply
\[
 \frac1{10}I\prec\Gamma(s)\prec4I,
 \qquad 0\le s\le1.
\]

For a coordinate or pair-sum ray \(u\in\mathcal R\),
\[
 |a^\top u|\in\left\{\frac25,1,\frac75,2\right\}.
\]
Writing \(r=|a^\top u|\), direct algebra gives, for \(t\ge1\),
\[
 \frac12\le\frac{(1+t)^2}{1+r^2t^2/2}
 \le\frac{27}{2}.
\]
The rational component and the lower bound on the splice multiplier yield
\[
 (1+t)^2|\phi_U(tu)|
 \ge\frac9{10}\cdot\frac12 e^{-2\kappa}
 =\frac9{20}e^{-1/10}>\frac25.
\]
For the upper envelope, write
\[
 (1+z)^2P_5(z)=\sum_k d_kz^k.
\]
Direct expansion gives \(\sum_k d_k k!=4714/63\).  Since
\(e^z\ge z^k/k!\), one has \(e^{-z}z^k\le k!\) for \(z\ge0\); and since \(r\ge2/5\),
\((1+t)^2\le(25/4)(1+rt)^2\).  Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (1+t)^2|\phi_U(tu)|
 &\le\frac9{10}\frac{27}{2}
   +\frac1{10}\frac{25}{4}\frac{4714}{63}\\
 &=\frac{37117}{630}<60.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The splice multiplier is at most one, so the same upper bound applies to both laws.  Evenness handles negative \(t\).  Thus every named ray has exponent two with common constants \(2/5\) and \(60\).

The scalar moment calculation gives \(\mathbb EH^8\le554293/90\) for either source used above.  If \(Z_3\sim N(0,I_3)\), then
\(\mathbb E\|Z_3\|^8=3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot9\).  Using
\(\|a\|_2^2=54/25\), \(\|\Gamma^{1/2}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\), and \((x+y)^8\le2^7(x^8+y^8)\), we get
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E\|aH+G_\Gamma\|^8
 &\le2^7\left\{
 \left(\frac{54}{25}\right)^4\frac{554293}{90}
 +4^4(3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot9)\right\}\\
 &<50000000.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Normalize each scalar source by its positive standard deviation and multiply its loading by that standard deviation.  This leaves \(U=aH\), its characteristic function, and the observational law unchanged, while producing a unit-variance source.  Since
\(\operatorname{Var}(H)\le41/45+1=86/45\), its adjusted loading satisfies
\[
 \|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
 \le\frac{54}{25}\frac{86}{45}
 =\frac{516}{125}<9,
\]
and hence \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}<3\).  It has rank one; its only column has positive first entry and is lexicographically sorted.  Positive variance gives nonconstancy, and Gaussian indecomposability is preserved by nonzero rescaling.

For an arbitrary \(u\in\mathbb R^3\), the source characteristic function along that direction is \(\phi_H(ta^\top u)\).  If \(a^\top u\ne0\), the two-sided polynomial bounds imply
\(\log|\phi_H(ta^\top u)|=O(\log|t|)\); if \(a^\top u=0\), that characteristic function is one.  Thus, for each constructed law,
\[
 -2t^{-2}\log|\phi_X(tu)|\longrightarrow u^\top\Gamma u.
\]
If \(\Delta\) is the covariance of any Gaussian convolution divisor of the same law, the residual characteristic function has modulus at most one, whence
\[
 e^{t^2u^\top\Delta u/2}|\phi_X(tu)|\le1.
\]
Taking logarithms, dividing by \(t^2/2\), and passing to the limit gives
\(u^\top\Delta u\le u^\top\Gamma u\) for every \(u\), so \(\Delta\preceq\Gamma\).  Since the displayed \(\Gamma\) is itself a Gaussian divisor in the construction, it is the greatest Gaussian-divisor covariance.

Finally, direct substitution along \(\Gamma(s)=\Gamma_\star+saa^\top\) gives
\[
 \Gamma_{WY}(s)
 -\frac{\Gamma_{WT}(s)\Gamma_{TY}(s)}{\Gamma_{TT}(s)}=0,
 \qquad
 \frac{\Gamma_{TY}(s)}{\Gamma_{TT}(s)}
 =\frac{3/5+s}{1+s}=b(s).
\]
Under the order whose only relation is \(T\prec Y\), the treatment-predecessor ideals are \(\varnothing\) and \(\{W\}\).  The first displayed equality makes the edge product in \(\mathrm{prop:ideal\text{-}fiber}\) vanish, while the second is the value for the empty ideal.  Hence
\[
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(s),\preceq)=\{b(s)\},
 \qquad 0\le s\le1.
\]
All additive, spectral, Fourier-envelope, moment, loading, rank, normalization, sign, order, greatest-divisor, and collision conditions have now been verified, so
\[
 P_{0,N},P_{1,N}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{col}}
 \subseteq\mathcal M_\star.
\]
By \(\mathrm{prop:lower\text{-}class\text{-}sr\text{-}inclusion}\), the same witnesses lie in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{SR}}\).  This completes the construction and all asserted limits.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every sufficiently large \(N\), there are Borel laws \(P_{0,N},P_{1,N}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{col}}\subseteq\mathcal M_\star\) and \(s_N=1/(600\log N)\) such that \(\Gamma(P_{0,N})=\Gamma(0)\), \(\Gamma(P_{1,N})=\Gamma(s_N)\), and \(\|P_{0,N}^{\otimes N}-P_{1,N}^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\to0\).  Both laws have a one-dimensional, unit-variance, Gaussian-indecomposable source representation with \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=1\) and \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}<3\), obey \(q_u=2\) on every \(u\in\mathcal R\) with common lower envelope constant \(2/5\) and upper envelope constant \(60\), satisfy \(\mathbb E\|X\|^8\le M_8=50000000\), and have the displayed covariance as their greatest Gaussian-divisor covariance.  Moreover,
\[
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P_{0,N}),\preceq)=\{b(0)\},\qquad
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P_{1,N}),\preceq)=\{b(s_N)\}.
\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The global loading-bound parameter is deleted. The witness theorem retains the same numerical strict loading bound directly inside the fixed lower subclass, so its claim must no longer mention the obsolete symbol.

proposed.name: Fourier-separated mixed-noise class
proposed.construction: \(\mathcal M(p,\lambda,\Lambda,c,C,Q,M_8,q,\preceq)=\{P_X:X=U+G_\Gamma,\ U=AH,\ U\perp G_\Gamma,\ \lambda I\preceq\Gamma\preceq\Lambda I,\ \Gamma\text{ is the greatest Gaussian divisor of }P_X,\ 1\le k\le p,\ H_1,\ldots,H_k\text{ are mutually independent, nonconstant, Gaussian-indecomposable, and unit variance},\ \operatorname{rank}(A)=k,\text{ the first nonzero entry of each column of }A\text{ is positive, the columns are in ascending lexicographic order},\ c(1+|t|)^{-q_u}\le|\phi_U(tu)|\le C(1+|t|)^{-q_u}\text{ for every }u\in\mathcal R\text{ and }|t|\ge1,\ \mathbb E\|X\|^8\le M_8,\ \preceq\text{ is a known strict partial order}\}\).

proposed.name: Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi observational class
proposed.construction:
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{SR}}\) is the class of centered observational laws \(P_X\) admitting a representation
\[
 X=AH+G_\Gamma,\qquad H\perp G_\Gamma,
\]
with \(1\le k\le p\), mutually independent coordinates \(H_1,\ldots,H_k\), \(\operatorname{Cov}(H)=I_k\), every \(H_j\) nonconstant and non-Gaussian and having no nondegenerate Gaussian convolution component, \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=k\), and the columns of \(A\) in ascending lexicographic order.  These are the observational restrictions in Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi Assumptions 2--4; no uniform Fourier envelope, spectral compactness, or eighth-moment bound is included in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{SR}}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The published class description is synchronized with the cap-free Fourier comparison and no longer suggests that loading compactness separates its scope from the upper results.

proposed.statement:
For every sufficiently large \(N\), there are Borel laws \(P_{0,N},P_{1,N}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{col}}\subseteq\mathcal M_\star\) and \(s_N=1/(600\log N)\) such that \(\Gamma(P_{0,N})=\Gamma(0)\), \(\Gamma(P_{1,N})=\Gamma(s_N)\), and \(\|P_{0,N}^{\otimes N}-P_{1,N}^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\to0\).  Both laws have a one-dimensional, unit-variance, Gaussian-indecomposable source representation with \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=1\) and \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}<3\), obey \(q_u=2\) on every \(u\in\mathcal R\) with common lower envelope constant \(2/5\) and upper envelope constant \(60\), satisfy \(\mathbb E\|X\|^8\le M_8=50000000\), and have the displayed covariance as their greatest Gaussian-divisor covariance.  Moreover,
\[
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P_{0,N}),\preceq)=\{b(0)\},\qquad
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P_{1,N}),\preceq)=\{b(s_N)\}.
\]

project_justification.niche: The upper and lower questions require different scopes. Honest finite-sample regions and upper rates are established on a fixed-dimensional class with known ordinary-smooth ray envelopes and compact spectral and moment bounds, without a global loading cap. The matching lower construction uses an explicit three-variable subclass that separately localizes \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le3\) and whose witnesses also satisfy the broader Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi published source hypotheses.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Source scales are normalized to unit variance, with full-column-rank, sign, and lexicographic loading conventions. No loading cap is imposed on the general Fourier or literal-Laplace upper classes; only the fixed lower subclass \(\mathcal M_\star\) requires \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le3\). The explicitly maintained greatest Gaussian-divisor covariance is recovered from centered empirical characteristic-function moduli on coordinate and pair-sum rays; the uniformly quantified literal-Laplace subclass instead uses clipped fourth cumulants and a global Lipschitz modulus.

prose_updates.related_work: Sanjaroonpouri and Ramazi are the population-identification anchor. Their Assumptions 2--4 use mutually independent nonconstant non-Gaussian sources with no Gaussian component, \(1\le k\le p\), unit covariance normalization, lexicographically ordered reduced-loading columns, and full column rank. The general Fourier class used for uniform inference adds known Fourier envelopes and compact spectral and moment restrictions, but no loading cap. The fixed exponent-two lower subclass separately imposes \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le3\), and its explicit splice witnesses satisfy the published hypotheses, so the logarithmic lower bounds transfer to the published class. No upper rate over the full published class is asserted. The greatest-Gaussian-divisor condition remains explicit in the Fourier model and is verified directly for the witnesses. Belomestny, Trabs, and Tsybakov supply the multivariate characteristic-function polarization precedent, and Meister supplies the scalar fixed-envelope centering and compensated lower-pair architecture; the present proof verifies the six-degree positivity, uniform derivatives, weighted Parseval bound, and causal collision embedding. Wang, Kolar, and Drton study recursive causally sufficient additive-error models and asymptotic coverage of one effect after order and adjustment-set inference; no blanket inclusion relation between their full model and the present one is used. Perkovi\'c, Kalisch, and Maathuis connect background knowledge to IDA effect multisets, while the CRAN \(\texttt{pcalg::ida}\) and Maathuis et al. yeast intervention-ranking workflow motivate reporting an honest compatible-effect set under an audited mixed-noise/Fourier model rather than a selected Gaussian-causal-sufficiency list. Miettinen, Taskinen, Nordhausen, and Oja provide the fourth-cumulant estimating-equation precedent for the literal-Laplace boundary.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The logarithmic upper guarantee is uniform only with fixed dimension and known ray exponents, Fourier envelopes, spectral bounds, and an eighth-moment bound; it does not require a global loading cap. The lower splice uses a fixed three-variable exponent-two class with the separate localization \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le3\) and conservative numerical constants. Its derivative and weighted-Parseval estimates establish product indistinguishability but do not provide adaptation to unknown smoothness or a matching upper theorem over the unrestricted Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi class.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The theorem-level deliverables are the exact ideal representation, collision-stable Lipschitz transfer, measurable finite-sample covariance and whole-fiber regions, \(O((\log N)^{-1})\) expected error on the cap-free Fourier class, the explicit positive smooth-splice pair, matching fixed-subclass minimax and honest-diameter results, lower-only transfer to the Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi class and every superclass containing the fixed splice class, and the uniformly quantified literal-Laplace boundary. The general Fourier and literal-Laplace upper results use no loading compactness; only \(\mathcal M_\star\) carries the direct bound \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le3\). No blanket nonnestedness theorem is claimed. The broader published class receives no upper-rate claim because it does not impose the uniform Fourier envelopes or compact spectral and moment bounds used by the estimator analysis. The proposal also does not claim adaptation to unknown exponents, growing-dimension guarantees, polynomial-delay ideal enumeration, correct singleton selection, or minimax sharpness for every exponent profile. When the partial order is total, the ideal family has one treatment-predecessor set and the fiber reduces to the usual singleton regression effect.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}\).  For a multi-index \(r=(r_1,\ldots,r_p)\in\mathbb N_0^p\) with \(1\le |r|:=\sum_i r_i\le4\), put \(Z_r=\prod_{i=1}^pX_i^{r_i}\), \(\mu_r=\mathbb E_P Z_r\), and \(\overline Z_r=N^{-1}\sum_{n=1}^N\prod_iX_{ni}^{r_i}\).  Let \(B=\sqrt{V_8}\), and let \(\widehat\mu_r=\operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}(\overline Z_r)\), as prescribed by \(\mathrm{def:laplace\mbox{-}region}\).  Since \(|Z_r|\le\|X\|^{|r|}\), the elementary inequality \(z^{2|r|}\le1+z^8\) for \(z\ge0\) and \(|r|\le4\), followed by \(\mathrm{ass:eighth\mbox{-}moment}\), gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P Z_r^2
 \le \mathbb E_P\|X\|^{2|r|}
 \le 1+\mathbb E_P\|X\|^8
 \le 1+M_8=V_8.
\]
Consequently \(|\mu_r|\le(\mathbb E_PZ_r^2)^{1/2}\le B\) by Cauchy--Schwarz.  Projection onto \([-B,B]\) cannot increase distance from the point \(\mu_r\in[-B,B]\), so
\[
 |\widehat\mu_r-\mu_r|\le|\overline Z_r-\mu_r|.
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:iid}\), \(\mathbb E_P(\overline Z_r-\mu_r)^2=N^{-1}\operatorname{Var}_P(Z_r)\le V_8/N\).  Summing over the \(d_4\) multi-indices therefore yields the uniform bound
\[
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2^2
 \le \frac{d_4V_8}{N}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Jensen's inequality applied to (1) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2
 \le \sqrt{\frac{d_4V_8}{N}},
 \tag{2}
\]
whereas Markov's inequality applied to the squared norm and the definition \(r_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}=\sqrt{d_4V_8/(N\alpha)}\) gives
\[
 P^{\otimes N}\!\left\{\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2>r_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}\right\}
 \le \frac{d_4V_8/N}{(r_N^{\mathrm{Lap}})^2}=\alpha.
 \tag{3}
\]

We next identify the value of the moment reconstruction at \(\mu\).  The centered standardized Laplace law has density \(f(h)=2^{-1/2}\exp(-\sqrt2|h|)\).  Symmetry gives mean zero, and direct integration using \(\int_0^\infty h^m e^{-ah}\,dh=m!a^{-(m+1)}\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E H_{\mathrm{Lap}}^2
 =\sqrt2\frac{2!}{(\sqrt2)^3}=1,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E H_{\mathrm{Lap}}^4
 =\sqrt2\frac{4!}{(\sqrt2)^5}=6.
\]
Its fourth cumulant is consequently \(6-3\cdot1^2=3\).  Under \(\mathrm{ass:laplace\mbox{-}source}\), \(U=a^{\mathrm{Lap}}H_{\mathrm{Lap}}\).  The additive model in \(\mathrm{def:laplace\mbox{-}model}\) makes this vector independent of the centered Gaussian component.  Additivity of joint cumulants for independent summands, multilinearity, and the vanishing of Gaussian cumulants of order four therefore imply, for every \(i\in V\),
\[
 \kappa_{TTTT}(X)=3(a_T^{\mathrm{Lap}})^4,
 \qquad
 \kappa_{iTTT}(X)=3a_i^{\mathrm{Lap}}(a_T^{\mathrm{Lap}})^3.
 \tag{4}
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:treatment\mbox{-}loading}\), \(|a_T^{\mathrm{Lap}}|\ge a_{\min}>0\).  Thus (4) gives \(\kappa_{TTTT}(X)\ge3a_{\min}^4>(3/2)a_{\min}^4\), so the positive floor in \(F_{p,M_8,a_{\min}}\) is inactive at \(\mu\), all divisions below have positive denominators, and
\[
 a_T(\mu)=|a_T^{\mathrm{Lap}}|,
 \qquad
 a_i(\mu)=\frac{3a_i^{\mathrm{Lap}}(a_T^{\mathrm{Lap}})^3}
 {3|a_T^{\mathrm{Lap}}|^3}
 =\operatorname{sgn}(a_T^{\mathrm{Lap}})a_i^{\mathrm{Lap}}.
 \tag{5}
\]
In particular, \(a(\mu)a(\mu)^\top=a^{\mathrm{Lap}}(a^{\mathrm{Lap}})^\top\).  Independence and unit variance of \(H_{\mathrm{Lap}}\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(X)
 =a^{\mathrm{Lap}}(a^{\mathrm{Lap}})^\top+\Gamma(P).
 \tag{6}
\]
Equations (5)--(6), together with \(\mathrm{ass:spectral\mbox{-}lower}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:spectral\mbox{-}upper}\), show that the matrix before spectral clipping equals \(\Gamma(P)\) and already has spectrum in \([\lambda,\Lambda]\).  Hence
\[
 F_{p,M_8,a_{\min}}(\mu)=\Gamma(P).
 \tag{7}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:laplace\mbox{-}region}\), \(\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}=F_{p,M_8,a_{\min}}(\widehat\mu)\).  Since both \(\mu\) and \(\widehat\mu\) belong to \([-\sqrt{V_8},\sqrt{V_8}]^{d_4}\), \(\mathrm{lem:laplace\mbox{-}global\mbox{-}lipschitz}\) and (7) give, for every sample outcome,
\[
 \|\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}-\Gamma(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_{\mathrm{Lap}}\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2.
 \tag{8}
\]
Combining (2) and (8), then taking the supremum over \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}\), proves the explicit uniform estimate
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}\|\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}-\Gamma(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_{\mathrm{Lap}}\sqrt{\frac{d_4V_8}{N}}.
 \tag{9}
\]
No loading-norm bound occurs in (1)--(9).

Spectral clipping ensures that \(\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}\) has spectrum in \([\lambda,\Lambda]\), while the same is true of \(\Gamma(P)\) by the two spectral assumptions.  Therefore \(\mathrm{lem:fiber\mbox{-}lipschitz}\), (8), and (2) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}
 d_H\!\left(\Theta_{TY}(\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}},\preceq),
             \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\right)\\
 &\hspace{25mm}\le L_\beta C_{\mathrm{Lap}}
 \sqrt{\frac{d_4V_8}{N}}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{10}
\]
This proves both asserted \(O(N^{-1/2})\) conclusions with constants independent of \(P\) and \(N\).

It remains to prove finite-sample whole-fiber coverage, including collision strata.  Define the event
\[
 \mathcal E_N=\left\{\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2\le r_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}\right\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal E_N\), (8) and \(\mathrm{lem:fiber\mbox{-}lipschitz}\) give
\[
 d_H\!\left(\Theta_{TY}(\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}},\preceq),
             \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\right)
 \le R_N,
 \qquad
 R_N:=L_\beta C_{\mathrm{Lap}}r_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}.
 \tag{11}
\]
By \(\mathrm{prop:ideal\mbox{-}fiber}\),
\[
 \Theta_{TY}(H,\preceq)=\{\beta_J(H):J\in\mathcal J\}
 \tag{12}
\]
for \(H=\Gamma(P)\) and for \(H=\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}\).  Thus, for every \(\theta\in\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\), the first directed term in the Hausdorff distance in (11) and (12) supply some \(J\in\mathcal J\) such that
\[
 |\theta-\beta_J(\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}})|\le R_N.
 \tag{13}
\]
There is no branch matching or separation step in this argument, so (13) remains valid when two or more ideal branches collide exactly.

We finally check that the terminal intersection with \([-\Lambda/\lambda,\Lambda/\lambda]\) in \(C_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}\) cannot delete a true effect.  Write \(S=D\cup J\).  By construction \(T\notin S\).  If \(Y\in S\), the partial covariance formula gives \(\gamma_{YT\cdot S}(\Gamma(P))=0\).  If \(Y\notin S\), the Schur complement of \(\Gamma(P)_{SS}\) is positive definite, so Cauchy--Schwarz for this conditional covariance matrix gives
\[
 |\gamma_{YT\cdot S}(\Gamma(P))|
 \le\sqrt{\gamma_{YY\cdot S}(\Gamma(P))
                 \gamma_{TT\cdot S}(\Gamma(P))}.
\]
The variational formula for a Schur complement and \(\lambda I\preceq\Gamma(P)\preceq\Lambda I\) yield
\[
 \gamma_{TT\cdot S}(\Gamma(P))\ge\lambda,
 \qquad
 \gamma_{YY\cdot S}(\Gamma(P))\le\Gamma(P)_{YY}\le\Lambda.
\]
Therefore, in either case,
\[
 |\beta_J(\Gamma(P))|
 \le\sqrt{\Lambda/\lambda}
 \le\Lambda/\lambda,
 \tag{14}
\]
where the last inequality uses \(0<\lambda<\Lambda\).  Equations (12)--(14) and the definition in \(\mathrm{def:laplace\mbox{-}region}\) imply on \(\mathcal E_N\) that
\[
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\subseteq C_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}.
\]
By (3), \(P^{\otimes N}(\mathcal E_N)\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}\); taking the infimum over \(P\) proves the advertised honest coverage for every \(N\).

For completeness, all constructions are measurable.  Empirical raw moments, coordinate projections, cumulant polynomials, the maximum with a positive constant, roots and reciprocal powers on the positive-floor domain, and spectral projection are Borel maps.  Matrix inversion is continuous on matrices bounded below by \(\lambda I\); \(\mathcal J\) is finite; and a finite union of compact intervals with Borel endpoints is a measurable random compact set.  Thus both estimators and the coverage event used above are well defined.  The proof uses the eighth-moment and treatment-loading restrictions, the spectral bounds, and the fixed compact moment map, but nowhere uses a bound on \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).

proposed.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}\), the fourth-cumulant construction satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}\|\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}-\Gamma(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(N^{-1/2})\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}d_H(\Theta_{TY}(\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}},\preceq),\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq))=O(N^{-1/2})\), and \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}}P^{\otimes N}\{\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\subseteq C_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(N\).
